overlap.title: Inheritance for daughters comes with a tribal marriage restriction

overlap.reasoning: The grant is significant within a male-priority succession system. The marriage limitation protects tribal landholding while restricting the beneficiaries’ choice; unrestricted equal inheritance is not stated.

overlap.title: The kinsman’s duty: buy the field “of Ruth”, or acquire Ruth?
overlap.summary: In the KJV Boaz tells the kinsman he must buy the field from Ruth as well as from Naomi. In the Septuagint he must also acquire Ruth herself.
overlap.reasoning: In the KJV wording of 4:5 the thing bought is the field, and Ruth is a second seller. In the Greek the kinsman must acquire two things: the field and “her”. Only the Greek wording of 4:5 states the duty that Boaz then says he has carried out in 4:10.
overlap.scope: The KJV follows the Hebrew words “and from Ruth” with no separate “her”; this is a Greek difference, not a claim that the KJV mistranslates the Hebrew. The Hebrew edition prints two forms of the verb (written and read); that marking is quoted for completeness and nothing is built on it. In every version the kinsman declines in 4:6 and Boaz marries Ruth. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient translation tradition, and the Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees, and neither edition settles which reading is earlier. overlap.title: Elimelech’s field: Naomi “selleth” it, or it “was given” to her?

overlap.title: Boaz to the kinsman: “if thou wilt not redeem” or “if he will not redeem”?
overlap.summary: The KJV has Boaz say to the kinsman “if thou wilt not redeem it”. The Hebrew verb is in the third person: “if he will not redeem”. The Septuagint agrees with the KJV.
overlap.reasoning: In the Hebrew the first verb is “thou wilt redeem” and the second, four words later, is “he will redeem”: two different forms side by side. The KJV prints “thou” for both. The Greek also has “thou” both times, so the Greek is not a difference from the KJV here.
overlap.scope: The sense of the conversation is not in doubt: Boaz is asking the kinsman for his decision, and the kinsman answers “I will redeem it”. The record is about the wording only: the KJV’s second “thou” matches the Greek and not the Hebrew of the named editions. Whether the Hebrew “he” is a slip, or Boaz turning to the elders for a moment, is not settled by the verse. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text, with the consonants-only Aleppo-based edition as a second witness. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined, and the KJV translators’ source for their wording is not established here. english.quote: to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance

Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.
So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.
And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it.
And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.

and Booz begat Obed of Ruth
